findings.what: AGENT.md §4 and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md (both language halves) place the maintainer's 2FA approval before the GitHub Release and GHCR in their sentence/arrow order, but the workflow creates the GitHub Release and pushes the GHCR image inside the same tag run, immediately after the stage step, with no human gate.
findings.where: AGENT.md §4 CI paragraph ('a maintainer approves the staged version with 2FA before it becomes live, then the GitHub Release is created and the GHCR image pushed'); .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md release-mapping paragraph ('tag -> npm stage publish ... -> maintainer 2FA approval + GitHub Release + GHCR') and its Chinese twin
findings.why: A maintainer may expect the Release/GHCR to be gated on the approval, and may be surprised that a GitHub Release exists while the npm version is not live. The package becoming live IS correctly gated on 2FA; only the sequencing narrative is off.
findings.direction: Describe the approval as asynchronous and separate from the run: the same run stages the package, creates the GitHub Release and pushes the GHCR image; a maintainer then approves the staged version with 2FA before it becomes live. Keep both language halves in sync.

declinedToJudge: Absolute wording 'Staging is always allowed for that trusted publisher' — read as a claim about the configured trusted publisher (npm's `npm trust ... --allow-stage-publish` is a per-relationship permission), consistent with the measured v0.7.1 denial; not a claim about npm globally.
Shorthand 'a direct npm publish needs --allow-publish' — `--allow-publish` is a real `npm trust <provider>` flag (verified in npm 11.19.0 docs); compressed but correct in context.
CHANGELOG keeps a '## 0.7.1 — 2026-10-30' section for a version that is not on the registry — the frozen requirement explicitly requires keeping 0.7.1 history, and Unreleased states the tag failed.

A re-run of the release workflow after a later GHCR/Release failure would try to stage the same version twice and hit the staged-version unique index — inherent to npm staged publishing, not introduced by this change, and not covered by the requirement.

The gate does not reject `working-directory` (or `shell`) on the publish step — the frozen gate contract enumerates the rejected modifiers, the current key allowlist is pre-existing, and the real workflow sets neither.
The GitHub Release is created before the npm version is live — the order is mandated by the frozen requirement (stage before Release), and the docs explain the approval.
The exact E403 log text quoted in CHANGELOG/README — the run metadata and the failed step are verified, the log body is not (logs API needs auth).
bounds: The real GitHub Actions v* tag run is UNPROVEN: no OIDC token exchange, no real staged publish, no provenance attestation and no 2FA approval were executed (no tag, no credentials, no maintainer approval). This remains unproven until the next tag run (v0.7.2) and its approval.
The exact E403 message in run 41019623710's log was not retrieved; only the run metadata and the failing step (step 20, 'Publish to npm (Trusted Publishing / OIDC)') were verified.
Did not run docker-verify.yml or boot-e2e.yml (Docker build, real harness boots); they are not in the §3 chain and this change set touches no plugin row or tool schema.
Did not measure the registry *install* path (needs a writable HOME/dsh profile).
The adversarial matrix and mutants lived under gitignored .tmp and were removed; the real .github/** was never written (workflow sha256 identical before and after).

Read the changed hunks, the release validator block, the self-test runner and all new fixtures, the PyYAML shape checks and the docs diffs; did not re-read every untouched line of the 1128-line gate script or the whole docs corpus.
The local bun is 1.4.2 while CI pins 1.4.3; tests passed locally and the workflow pin is unchanged and still asserted by the gate.

The copy-based old-gate cross-check used HEAD's gate script with symlinked scripts/ and Dockerfile; the new gate rejects the old release.yml and the old gate rejects the new one (both exit 1, release-npm-publish).
verdictJustification: Every frozen requirement was observed by running it: the release workflow carries the exact staged step in the required position with the three write permissions and no token path, the gate passes 4/4 and rejects every adversarial variant (plain publish, --dry-run, if, continue-on-error, env, with, id-token removal, both order moves, duplicates, echo/||/extra-line) while its self-test is an honest 38/38 that grew by exactly the one new control, the §3 chain is 11/11 with 325 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail and no secret material, and the bilingual docs/CHANGELOG/PR template are in sync with no 0.7.2 claim; the only observation is one non-blocking Nit about approval/Release sequencing in AGENT.md and the PR template, and the real stage publish + 2FA approval remain a stated bound until the next tag run.
